tools.name: ip_lookup
tools.description: Look up geolocation, ISP and network info for any IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname, or an array of them for batch lookup. Returns ip, city, region, country, coordinates, ASN/ISP, timezone and continent (full name, e.g. North America); when a domain is queried, an extra `domain` field echoes it. Data so

tools.name: ip_resolved
tools.description: Resolve a domain to all its A and AAAA records (deduplicated, up to 6) and return geolocation for each address. Returns an array of { ip, protocol, domain, city, region, country, coordinates, ASN/ISP, ... }. For a bare IP, returns a single-element array.

tools.name: ip_self
tools.description: Get geolocation and network info about the caller's own public IP, plus the protocol stack (IPv4/IPv6) of the current connection. tools.name: headers
tools.description: Return all HTTP request headers as seen by the IP.LS server (including X-Real-IP / X-Forwarded-For injected by the frontend proxy). Useful for debugging proxies and client identity.

tools.name: ua
tools.description: Return the User-Agent string of the current HTTP client.

tools.name: ip_summary
tools.description: Summarize a large batch of IPs into distributions by country, continent, ASN/operator and network prefix, each bucket with a sample of addresses. Use instead of ip_lookup once the input is in the hundreds or thousands — ip_lookup returns every row, which no context window holds. Up to 5000 addresses

findings.title: Description tells the model to hide behavior
findings.detail: Description of "ip_summary" instructs the model to conceal actions from the user.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "ip_summary" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Aggregate a batch of up to 5000 IPv4/IPv6 addresses (or up to 100 hostnames, each resolved server-side) into deterministic distributions by country, continent, ASN/operator and network prefix, each bucket carrying a bounded sample so the result can be spot-checked without re-running the batch. Count" → after: "Summarize a large batch of IPs into distributions by country, continent, ASN/operator and network prefix, each bucket with a sample of addresses. Use instead of ip_lookup once the input is in the hundreds or thousands — ip_lookup returns every row, which no context window holds. Up to 5000 addresses"

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
